title: Optimization and Complexity of Inertia-Type Bounds on the Independence Number: the equivalence of the two mixed-integer formulations (Theorem 3.2)
author: Aida Abiad, Stan van Hoesel, Valentin Michaux
work: Optimization and Complexity of Inertia-Type Bounds on the Independence Number
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's equivalence theorem for its two mixed-integer formulations of the k-independence number, printed as Theorem 3.2 at source0.tex lines 437-448 and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 450-490). The statement has two halves: the optima of the two formulations coincide, the second optimum being the minimum over the vertices of the first formulation's optimum, and every feasible solution of the second formulation can be transformed into a feasible solution of the first at some vertex without changing its binary variables or its objective value. The proof is the paper's own: it reconstructs the auxiliary variables of the first formulation from those of the second, shows feasibility of the reconstruction, compares the two objective functions term by term including the incentive term that distinguishes the formulations, and completes the equality of optima in both directions. This is a research-level polyhedral-combinatorial argument about integer programming formulations of a graph-spectral bound rather than a qualifying-examination exercise; the unit is H2.
